pages.title: What is Inheritance
pages.content: Inheritance allows a subclass to reuse members of a superclass with the `extends` keyword. A subclass can directly use inherited methods and add its own behavior.

callout.title: Key takeaway
callout.text: Inheritance lets a subclass reuse and extend superclass behavior.

checkpoint.question: Which feature allows a subclass to provide its own implementation of an inherited method?
checkpoint.explanation: Method overriding lets a subclass redefine an inherited instance method.

pages.title: What is Polymorphism
pages.content: Polymorphism allows a superclass reference to refer to a subclass object. With method overriding, the subclass implementation is selected at runtime.

callout.title: Key takeaway
callout.text: Overridden methods enable runtime polymorphism.

pages.title: Why this concept matters
pages.content: Inheritance models an is-a relationship and enables reuse plus specialization. Polymorphism then lets parent references work with child objects.

questions.question: Which is a widening conversion?
questions.explanation: int to double is widening.

questions.question: What happens to 3.9 in `(int)3.9`?
options: The fraction is discarded and result is 3
questions.explanation: Narrowing cast truncates the fractional part.

questions.question: Why does double-to-int require an explicit cast?
questions.explanation: Narrowing can lose range or precision.

questions.question: Which method parses String to int?
questions.explanation: Integer.parseInt converts valid integer text.

questions.question: Which method parses String to double?
questions.explanation: Double.parseDouble parses decimal text.

questions.question: What does instanceof test?
questions.explanation: instanceof checks whether an object is compatible with a reference type.

questions.question: What can happen when an Animal holding a Cat is cast to Dog?
questions.explanation: An incompatible downcast throws ClassCastException.

questions.question: Does a cast transform the actual object?
options: No, it only changes how the reference is treated if valid
questions.explanation: A cast does not transform the object.

questions.question: What does integer division use when both operands are int?
questions.explanation: The result is an integer quotient.

questions.question: Why can double-to-float conversion change displayed digits?
questions.explanation: float has fewer precision bits than double.
